label: PRIORITY SUBMISSION REVIEW; user-supplied score associations are not organizer-confirmed
source_method: Repository-pinned raster forensic records plus the current user-supplied site list; one public leaderboard page fetch in this session.

decision.reason: No listed TIFF has a receipt binding the claimed score to its exact bytes, and none is approved by the separate selector under a fresh comparable buffered holdout. The highest reported artifact is historical and is not a new unique candidate.
decision.current_public_leaderboard_observation: 0.4413 displayed in the first public row on 2026-10-26; this is not a receipt for a local raster and does not identify a file that can be copied or reproduced.

sites.review: H19-5 probability surface with d=1.5 thinning. Against the next H19-5 d=2.8 result the reported score rises while the dot count falls, consistent with greater emission efficiency but not proof of hidden-truth causation.
H19-5 d=2.8 thinned raster. Its pixel set is byte-for-byte dot-identical to the GEMSDOE30 d28 artifact in the pinned forensic audit; therefore these are not independent algorithmic confirmations.

Topology gap-closure variant on a d=1.5 base. The reported result is below the H19-5 d=2.8 and solo results despite the larger dot count; this cannot distinguish useful fault additions from false positives without held-out truth.
Highest score reported for this site in the user's list. It is only 6 dots above the H33-2-B2 count, but similar count is not identity and does not establish similar predictions.
The pinned forensic audit finds the same dot set as GEMSDOE25's H19-5 d=2.8 raster; this is a cross-site replication of bytes, not a second independent model result.
The pinned forensic audit finds the same solo-r1 set at GEMSDOE28. GEMSDOE32's 37,654-dot set is this solo raster after removing 2,545 catalogue-flank dots; it adds no predictions.

Highest reported result in the nine-site list. Exact pixel audit: solo-r1 minus the catalogue-distance <=2-pixel ring; 2,545 dots removed, zero added, zero reconstruction difference. This supports a precision/emission-hygiene explanation conditional on the reported ladder, not score causation or a new detector.

The pinned forensic audit measures 31,614 exact shared dots with the GEMSDOE32 raster: 75.5% of this artifact's dots. That exceeds the protocol's >70% within-3-pixel duplicate threshold against that registry raster; it is not a unique-candidate template.

The pinned forensic audit finds the GEMSDOE32 set plus 1,200 dots. Thus 37,654/38,854 = 96.9% of its dots exactly overlap the GEMSDOE32 raster, above the protocol's >70% duplicate threshold; the reported PINN name does not establish independent predictions.

leaderboard_observation.method: One fetch of the public HTML leaderboard in this session; no authentication, upload, or submission-page receipt.
leaderboard_observation.scope_limit: A public leaderboard row is an official page observation but does not associate the score with any raster in GEMSDOE24/25/27/28/30/31/32/33/36. The page is dynamic; this is a dated snapshot.

hypotheses.name: Displaced potential-field piercing markers
hypotheses.layers: Cached RTP/TMI and isostatic-gravity anomaly bands; LiDAR strike/validity only as an independent support mask.
hypotheses.physical_signature: Register paired magnetic/density marker ridges on opposite sides of a candidate corridor; require at least two coherent lateral offsets with a consistent direction and support the intervening corridor rather than the displaced contacts.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_reason: A structure may offset pre-existing magnetic/density contacts without a mapped Quaternary surface scarp; use no catalogue-tip interpolation and no copied raster dots.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: No paired-marker registration/displacement transform found in the reviewed modules. Distinct from Euler source-depth estimates, upward-continuation ridge migration, ordinary edge co-location and catalogue-gap closure.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Cross-cutting intrusive contacts, branching lithologic contacts, or survey-registration seams.
hypotheses.expected_benefit: Highest qualitative information potential in this four-item slate; no numeric projection or measured DTI.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high; require registration-quality and seam/placebo controls.
hypotheses.data_status: Existing cached bands were restored and hash-verified in the prior S18 run; owner-mirror integrity is not organizer authentication. No new external bytes required for the first test.
hypotheses.status: Proposed only; no implementation or holdout result in this review; no global novelty claim.

hypotheses.name: Lithology-conditioned uranium/thorium transport dipoles
hypotheses.layers: GeoDAWN K, Th, U radiometry / U-Th ratio and isostatic-gravity edge orientation.
hypotheses.physical_signature: Odd-symmetric, cross-corridor U/Th residual conditioned on local Th and K, persistent along strike while bulk lithologic contrast is weak; test missingness and quantization separately.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_reason: Fluid/redox transport along a concealed permeable boundary could alter mobile uranium relative to thorium without preserving a surface scarp; this is a conjecture, not a geothermal detector claim.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Tests signed dipole morphology and a lithology-conditioned residual, unlike scalar radiometric values/ratios, ridge conjunctions, or the earlier magnetic-trough/Th-K depletion proposal.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Groundwater redox fronts, surficial sediment sorting, radon disequilibrium, or airborne survey artifacts.
hypotheses.expected_benefit: Moderate qualitative potential; high physical ambiguity; no numeric projection or measured DTI.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium; quantized raster inputs cannot support absolute geochemical calibration.
hypotheses.data_status: Source bands are recorded in the GeoDAWN and GDR inventories, but original official bytes have not been independently downloaded in this review; owner-mirror hashes do not authenticate provenance.
hypotheses.status: Proposed only; no implementation or holdout result in this review; no global novelty claim.

hypotheses.name: Paired-geothermometer cooling corridors
hypotheses.layers: INGENIOUS GDR well/spring coordinates, measured temperatures, paired quartz/chalcedony geothermometer estimates, plus magnetic/gravity geometry.
hypotheses.physical_signature: After deduplicating source sites, test persistent directional differences between reservoir-temperature estimates and measured temperatures along a multi-site corridor, not a circular hot-spring buffer.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_reason: A connected upflow/discharge path may lack a mapped surface rupture; paired cooling/disequilibrium may supply evidence not present in a single high-temperature threshold.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Retains paired temperatures and directional site-to-site structure; differs from the thermal module's maximum-geothermometer and near-site distance thresholds and the earlier vent/spring halo experiment.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Groundwater mixing, incomplete mineral equilibration, drilling/production effects, or preferential sampling.
hypotheses.expected_benefit: Low-medium qualitative priority owing to sparse, biased point support; no numeric projection or measured DTI.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium; deduplicate measurements and pass site-density/leakage canaries.
hypotheses.data_status: Official GDR #1391 listing and well/spring archive link are publicly visible; the linked archive bytes, CRS, coverage and transformed owner mirror were not re-downloaded/authenticated here. Thus not data-ready for a holdout run.
hypotheses.status: Proposed only; holdout blocked on data-byte/schema/coverage re-verification; no global novelty claim.

hypotheses.name: Opposite-flank flexural curvature pairs
hypotheses.layers: Detrended elevation, LiDAR upface/downface/relief/strike/validity descriptors, and long-wavelength isostatic gravity.
hypotheses.physical_signature: Ordered signed broad-curvature lobes on opposite sides of a corridor with consistent relief asymmetry, separating broad warping from a sharp scarp response.
hypotheses.off_catalogue_reason: Distributed flexure above a buried normal fault could persist where no sharp mapped surface break occurs; scalar layers alone do not establish dip or slip.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Tests ordered opposite-flank pairs rather than the existing gradient strength, local relief or unsigned curvature magnitude.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Alluvial-fan margins, paleoshorelines, differential compaction, lithology-controlled erosion or raster seams.
hypotheses.expected_benefit: Lowest of this slate due to abundant geomorphic mimics; no numeric projection or measured DTI.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium for coarse screening; higher for full-resolution confirmation.
hypotheses.data_status: Coarse feature bands are available from prior hash-verified owner mirrors. A high-resolution validation would require USGS 3DEP tiles; tile availability/coverage was not checked in this review, so no high-resolution experiment is proposed as viable yet.
hypotheses.status: Proposed only; no implementation or holdout result; global novelty is unproven.
